title: Granny square pullover
excerpt: A classic pullover assembled entirely from 15 cm granny squares. Each square is worked separately then joined with slip stitch seams. The square count determines the fit. Graded XS to 2XL.
sourceNotes: Granny square garments are a long-established technique in crochet. Construction logic is standard.

glossaryTerms.definition: A classic motif worked in rounds from a centre ring. Each round adds a shell of dc or treble clusters at the corners and along each side, building a flat square.
A method of joining finished motifs by placing them wrong sides together and working a slip stitch through both outer loops along the shared edge. The result is a flat visible seam on the right side.
Wetting or steaming a finished piece and pinning it to measurements while it dries. Granny squares block reliably and all four corners sharpen to 90 degrees.

crochet.gaugeText: Each granny square measures 15 x 15 cm blocked.
crochet.finishedSizeText: XS to 2XL. Size M: adjust square count as noted in pattern.

content.text: This pullover is built entirely from
The finished garment has a relaxed drop-shoulder fit. Size comes from how many squares you use in each panel, not from row-count adjustments.

Each square is 15 cm. At size M, the front and back panels are each 4 squares wide and 4 squares tall (60 x 60 cm). Each sleeve is 3 squares wide and 4 squares tall (45 x 60 cm). Total squares needed at size M: 56.

To go up or down a size, add or remove one square column from both front and back panels. XS: 3 wide x 4 tall per body panel. S: 3 wide x 4 tall. M: 4 wide x 4 tall. L: 4 wide x 4 tall with one border square added at each side. XL: 5 wide x 4 tall. 2XL: 5 wide x 4 tall with one border square added at each side.
Round 1: Magic ring, ch 3 (counts as first tr), 2 tr into ring, ch 2, [3 tr, ch 2] three times. Join with sl st.
Round 2: Sl st to corner ch-2 sp, ch 3, 2 tr in same sp, ch 1, [3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr] in next corner sp, ch 1. Repeat around. Join.
Round 3: Sl st to corner sp, ch 3, 2 tr in same sp, ch 1, 3 tr in ch-1 sp, ch 1, [3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr] in corner sp. Repeat around. Join and fasten off.

Block every square before assembly. Lay out the front panel squares in a grid and join each pair of adjacent edges with a flat join, working row by row. Join the back panel the same way. Sew shoulder seams. Attach sleeve panels at the armhole edges, then seam sleeve and side edges from hem to cuff.
Work one round of dc around the neck opening to neaten the edge. Fasten off and weave in ends.
The granny square cardigan uses the same square and the same join. The only difference is the front panels are left open and finished with a dc border.
